## Design

### 2026-10-13 – # making basic items for my Fishbl!

**1h**

# making basic items for my Fishbl!

### Idea
I started out by coming up with an idea for my Merbl run, because I truly wanted it to be much more customized than the Starbie I made last week. I came up with having it based around a theme, and I decided on fishes. So, I can make certain parts of the Merbl run more customizable and I don't have to spend so much time thinking about what to customize, since I already have a theme in mind! For example, I can change the pins in the Plinko track to be seaweed. I was also inspired by Whitney's gym in Pokemon Gold and Silver that is based around a Clefairy, but you can really only tell from the top-down. So, I want my Merbl run to literally be in the shape of a fish, but I don't want it to be too immediately obvious, and only from the top view downward.

I also plan to make more custom items if I have more time, since I'm a little bit more experienced in CAD compared to PCBs. I already have a starting line, custom edges to the tracks, and other unique track ideas in mind!

### Work
For today, I started out by signing up for Onshape and creating the basic track. I've never used Onshape so it was definitely a bit of a learning curve, but I have worked with other sort of similar softwares (mainly Sketchup) so I know some of the functions. One of the things I struggled with was knowing what a "sketch" was. I know what a plane is and I get the idea of a sketch (a 2D image that you can extrude to turn 3D), but for some reason my sketch kept disappearing and the guide wasn't too clear on that, so I had to watch several Youtube videos. I also didn't get why my dimensions weren't in millimeters, so I also had to watch on how to change that. All in all, it took me quite some time to get to this stage:

![Screenshot 2026-10-13 005306](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/d7f6c4083a7120bd3f2d91e8732a6c5c249cbca868e172f3c108ffd4cde55950.png)

The rest of making the basic track went pretty smoothly because CAD pretty much only has a few basic functions that you can combine to create any shape you want, then just extrude it. I already have ideas of what else I want to make to customize the Fishbl!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/2ba84791f9a8a6f9abcb67585cabb7deb58e21ffe46f369b2270d93f3dc6528d.png)

tl;dr is that I came up with the idea for my Merbl run (Fishbl), and then spent some time getting used to Onshape and making the basic track & base

### 2026-10-14 – # creating more advanced paths!

**1.75h**

# creating more advanced paths!

I started off this session by just creating some basic notes so I have a better understanding of all the functions in OnShape. I'll also refer to it later when I'm creating my actual projects instead of each of the individual components!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/a2ab04bcdebd63a25d104da93250763e34de4279f78066bf44aaae6b60ffb8da.png)

After making the basic track yesterday, I moved on to making curved tracks today. The guide showed both ways of doing this, and I tried out both ways, though they were equally confusing. Most of my confusion came from the dimensions used in the guide, since, when I used them in Onshape, it would say that to make such dimensions was geometrically impossible. For the first method of creating a curved track, which uses a fillet, the guide mentioned the radius should be at least 12 mm, but the 20 mm line that was meant to create this fillet was too small to accommodate it. Forcing it to be 20 mm would create a weird extra gap.

![Screenshot 2026-10-14 001522](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/56356ddbc8f3b0d4ab95a883e646cda575a00ebbad7e9ecb868af6a00886577f.png)

I tried to make the 20 mm line longer, and it required a 33 mm line in order to accomodate a 12 mm circle (fillet). Then, I realized that the guide screenshot showed the radius as 7 mm, even though it specifically mentioned 12 mm? Regardless, 7 mm worked perfectly, so I decided to use that instead of the 12 mm. However, when I sweeped it, the 7 mm was too small and resulted in the path crashing into itself or creating this weird shape (yellow line is what I WANT the path to look like:

![screenshot12](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/058e55c3c0e85d6360b2b26e2d1d170c344c71a854ab4cce4b59e78257b26012.png)

I eventually moved on to the second method because I spent lots of time already researching on why it didn't work, but I'll try again tomorrow.  The second method, which uses a composite curve, was much easier. The only confusing part is that the text in the guide doesn't really match with the screenshots, but the screenshots are much more helpful. For example, the text says to make the radius of the curve 20 mm, but the screenshot shows the diameter as 54 mm (which would result in a radius of 27 mm, not 20 mm). When I tried using 20 mm, an error popped up saying that the sweep failed because it crashed into itself, so I switched to using the 27 mm circle. This worked well, but I also found it easier to use arcs instead of making circles and trimming the excess side. After a lot of effort, I was able to get here!

![Screenshot 2026-10-14 004651](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/b6a5f813caeb350900005dd67e2e4cf3f5d5ca1854c33d4ed3b946b51bc45861.png)

tl;dr is that I created some notes for Onshape, then spent some time making curved paths but was confused with the dimension differences in the guide

### 2026-10-14 – # Making some custom paths!

**1.58h**

# Making some custom paths!

One of the most fun parts of Merbl are the custom paths that you can make! The guide provides you with 3 custom paths that you can use as assets in the marble run, so I made them for this session. The first one was the Plinko, which was the hardest to make out of all 3 (I spent 40 minutes setting up most of the sketch before I started recording for the timelapse, so that's why there's 0.66 hours in this entry), but it also used the useful tools coincident and mirror, which I also used frequently through the next two paths.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/d8c59fa424ba89a8c5d5be8e83e99eb4d2f37e54fd1db627db67cc4a96b21be0.png)

What was especially difficult in making the Plinko was the fact that there were so many lines to construct it. Sometimes, when making a line on top of another line, Onshape treats it as just one line. So, if I had to get a dimension for the line on top, it would try to give me the dimension of the entire line, which was super unhelpful. Instead, I ended up making the lines off the main line, and then connect them using Coincident.

The staircase was the second easiest, since it just required copy and pasting stairs. The guide said to use the equal tool and dimension tool, but I found it easier to just copy and paste lots of stairs and then connect them using Coincident. The only part I didn't understand was the extruding, since the guide said to use Opposite, but I found it was easier to just make 2 extrusions and offset 1.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/53f398200430db33f3c9ca743d95c7b8a766d50b8511ec0d09a705fd586aa6e3.png)

Finally, the funnel was by far the easiest. All I had to do was make a sketch and round the corners using Fillet, then just revolve it!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/1efaaf316710259ab8a585d3bc08bee3748014b9ae2106791ef57527d3d55617.png)

Though I might not use all these assets in the future, I'll still definitely use the tools (especially Revolve, Coincident, and Mirror) when making my Fishbl.

tl;dr is that I created the custom paths listed in the guide and learned Coincident, Mirror, and Revolve

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/31fff6ec-5e14-4577-a323-da62f17e6ec1/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-15 – # failed idea...

**1h**

# failed idea...

Though I did want to make a fish-shaped marble run, I realized it would be far too difficult to actually make it and make it look good, especially because I'm on a time limit. I started out by drawing what I wanted my Merbl to look like:

![Screenshot 2026-10-14 232202](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/633232783dfac1570dc91de69a578b0f05ddde8a293695f7f9be021ac13b82c8.png)

My idea was to create 4 separate planes and then draw each of these items on there, as shown here:

![Screenshot 2026-10-14 235249](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/1b7e17ee0d018dae3adf461114aebe23427a89530c19d9e5dea739c3db80e066.png)

However, I soon realized I can't just draw flat paths because the marble wouldn't move at all, and would require a lengthy ramp in order to gain enough momentum. I tried to make the layers slightly curve downwards, but, because my fish design has lots of curves in it, it would be too difficult to turn the fish design into multiple pieces, angle them all individually, create a sketch for each, and connect them all. I spent a lot of time trying to get my design to work, but I think it's a little too complicated for me to make right now, but I'll definitely be attempting this a second time in the future.

Instead, I'll be utilizing a helix which naturally spirals downward in a smooth motion for my next design. It won't be shaped like a fish, but I'll still add multiple fish elements since I want to stick to that idea.

tl;dr is that I decided not to go with the fish-from-above marble run design because it would be too complicated to angle each part, so I decided to make my design a helix instead.

### 2026-10-15 – # making the base  of my NEW fishbl!

**1.7h**

# making the base  of my NEW fishbl!

Like I said before, I wanted to make my new Fishbl in a helix shape. I watched several videos online of marble runs, and the swirly part that was at the top or bottom was always my favourite part because it's super satisfying to watch the marble go through the loops. So, I decided to make my Fishbl entirely the helix, and it also naturally spirals downward so I don't have to worry about angling everything correctly. It isn't really a race any more and more of a tabletop desktoy, but I think it'll be much more stress relieving than other marble runs.

Onshape already has a built in helix tool, so I used that and sweeped in the path.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/9aa3bf37ed4b95cbdb06db2251008d3ab86c611ba0322a8c6d84b516155e0a21.png)

I also added a pole in the middle to support everything and two stars at the end for the start and end of the run. It also has a flat trough at the top for the marbles to rest on. I'm going to add a simple push mechanism to push the marbles that are resting on the trough for some more functionality.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/0989bc30a5add2dfc050dd054cc09efb6c97ff3e062d0991416bda53692bfd8a.png)

I also designed this tiny fish charm to add onto the pole with magnets, making it look like a tiny aquarium!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/b683e15a4b76efa0bce74dedab870724e883e867ce29cb95f70eef2417db72d8.png)

(this is what I mean)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/6242f23c4a909357079d7c33db0506b765f6a2800918e519729dea52d3bd8333.png)

tl;dr is that I designed the basic base of my Fishbl, and I'll continue adding details on it such as charms and functionality!

### 2026-10-16 – # making some more charms!

**1h**

# making some more charms!

I want the tower to have a sort of scrapbook-y feel, so I decided to make some more filler charms, like the   star and shell. In general, I made the charms smaller compared to my original fish charm, since I wanted more space to put it. I also wasn't entirely happy with the appearance of the squid, jellyfish, or shrimp that I made in the last entry, since I thought they didn't match the style too well. So I remade them into a clownfish, starfish, and pufferfish! I went through several iterations with these charms because I wanted them to look cohesive and recognizable, so it took lots of tweaking and editing to get to this stage.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/b5c20cb8df229b5d8a7b23d42f1a74671ee835f677e2fb340120c28cc2af9091.png)

I also plan to add magnets in the back of the charms so that you can add, remove, and interchange them freely on the tower, so I added holes in the back. I made sure to account for tolerances though, making them ~.2 mm larger than the magnets actually are.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/0dadf27792efcf7dac8aba39472efb33fb8e4a003cf331e10597e91719e93f4b.png)

Next, I want to add the magnet holes onto the actual tower and clean up everything for submission!

tl;dr is that I updated the charms and added magnet holes in the back of them

### 2026-10-17 – # finishing my Fishbl!

**1.1h**

# finishing my Fishbl!

I finished the base of my Fishbl by adding in all the magnet holes! I did this by creating tangent planes that surrounded the middle cylinder, and then drawing circles onto them using their sketches. I found out about the wrap tool, which helps wrap sketches onto 3D curves, such as the cylinder! It was so much easier adding all the holes this way, since now I don't have to worry about how different depths are required for curves on a 2D plane.

![Screenshot 2026-10-16 233930](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/3f5229a7b258815d1389dc813c249aced2fd141a33ab0b9e407a7cf21f9d41e8.png)

I also wanted to add the charms onto the pole so I could see what it looked like, mostly for aesthetic purposes (and for the cover of the project) rather than actual functionality, since I'm going to printing the charms separate from the cylinder anyways. However, since it's a curved surface, it's a lot more complicated than I thought it was. I tried to use the same method I did with the holes but add extruding instead of remove extruding, but the charms didn't look right and also became fused with the pole. Then, I tried to use mate connectors, but for some reason the charms just weren't rotated correctly.

![Screenshot 2026-10-17 003129](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/daf354c993ae6bf9a03472b884f998f911c6aeb0e17035409bb2f4519344b923.png)

I tried to use the rotate functions built into the mate connector transform tool, but it only rotated on the Z-axis, not the X or Y axis I needed it to be. I also tried to change the location of the mate connector, which worked, but only for magnet holes that are direct 90 degree angles from the center axis. Eventually, I decided it wasn't really worth it to try to get everything aligned perfectly if it was just for aesthetic purposes, so I simply transformed everything until it was about the right position.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/1dbdab88c63059abea76590c18a0067797b37a43e8a73873b7ef1ae25308e81c.png)

Now you can see my idea come to life! I'll be able to adjust everything and rotate everything correctly once I have it in-person, but I can see approximately how it'll look for one side now.

tl;dr is that I added the magnet holes, and I tried to add charms onto them but it wasn't rotated correctly, so I just transformed them without bothering with rotation
